tagline: Dinner, coffee and the dog run are on foot, and your parents are close.
subhead: Old city blocks where dinner, coffee and the dog run are a walk away and the car mostly rests.
scene: You work at home in an old city building, with a supermarket 0.1 miles away. The evening dog walk reaches a park in about 5 minutes, and a dog run is 0.4 miles off. On Saturday you walk to dinner: about 29 restaurants, 6 bars and 8 cafés sit within a 10-minute walk. The car mostly waits. On Sunday the typical place here is about 16 minutes from your parents by car, or about 30 by transit.
promise: Nearly everything you want in an evening is a walk from your door.
catch: 68 percent of households here have no car, so easy parking is the hard part. The list is short, with 6 places in all.
host_intro: You close the laptop, clip on the leash, and everything you want from the evening is within reach of your front door. This is old city living, where most households do without a car and yours would rest for days. It suits you if going out is the point.
host_walkthrough:
Morning starts with the dog. A park is about 5 minutes from the door and a dog run about 0.4 miles, so the early loop is short. Coffee is a walk too. You work from home, and when the walls close in, a supermarket sits about 0.1 miles away. The car keys can stay on the hook until the weekend.

Saturday night is why you came. Dinner is a walk, the next stop is a walk, and within 1 mile there are about 111 restaurants to work through. Nobody has to be the driver. The catch waits at the curb: if the car went out, coming home late means circling for a spot. Ask every building where it sleeps.

Sunday dinner at your parents' is the easy part. The drive is about 16 minutes from the typical place, and about 5 from the closest, Kew Gardens, with no tolls on the typical drive. Transit works as a backup at about 30 minutes. You can stay for seconds and still be home before the dog starts filing complaints.
sub_cost: Most of your budget goes to the monthly bill here.
sub_to_parents: Your parents stay part of the week.
sub_going_out: Restaurants and bars are both in walking reach.
sub_green: The dog's daily loop can include a park.
sub_compared_to_queens: About what Queens gives you on foot, a little farther from home.

Saturday night is strong on food and thinner on bars. There are about 66 restaurants within 1 mile, and the bars within a 10-minute walk number about 2. Dinner is local. Then the car. Only about 37 percent of places here list a garage or covered spot, so know where it sleeps before you sign.

Sunday is where this experience pays you back. Your parents are about 24 minutes from the typical place, and about 2 from the closest, Jamaica. The typical drive has no tolls, though the priciest crossing here runs about $43 round trip with a New York E-ZPass. Close enough to drop by. Close enough that they might, too.

tagline: A downtown of your own, a garage, and a real drive home.
subhead: Small downtowns with a train station close by, a garage for the car and a real drive home.
scene: You work at home in a small city or inner suburb, with a train station about 0.5 miles away. The evening dog walk reaches a park in about 7 minutes, and the dog park is about 1.2 miles off. On Saturday the downtown has about 7 restaurants within a 10-minute walk and 17 within 1 mile. Most households keep a car. On Sunday the typical place here is about 52 minutes from your parents by car, or about 105 by transit.
promise: A downtown of your own, and a car for everything else.
catch: Your parents are about 52 minutes from the typical place. Bars are thin, about 1 within a 10-minute walk, so a real night out often means driving.
host_intro: Think a downtown you can learn in a month and a building that takes the car seriously. For someone who wants to pull in at night and stop thinking about the car, that matters. What you give up is a little size and a lot of closeness: dropping by becomes a plan.
host_walkthrough:
On a weekday the dog gets a park about 7 minutes away. The proper dog park is about 1.2 miles off, so that is a drive or a long walk. Then coffee downtown, work at home, and groceries about 0.4 miles away. Most of these buildings have a gym downstairs, which helps in February.

Saturday night, the downtown does its job. About 7 restaurants sit within a 10-minute walk and about 17 within 1 mile. Bars are the thin spot, about 1 close by, so the bigger night is a ride away. Coming home is the good part. At most of these places you pull into the garage and the day is over.

Sunday takes commitment. The typical drive to your parents is about 52 minutes each way without traffic, or about 27 from the closest, Long Beach. Tolls run about $17 round trip with a New York E-ZPass. Transit is about 105 minutes, so the car is the real answer. You will go. You will also check traffic first.
sub_to_parents: A real drive home, so visits get planned.
sub_going_out: Some places to eat nearby, and more by car.
sub_green: A park is close enough for daily walks.
sub_compared_to_queens: Farther out than Queens, with less on foot.

tagline: More square feet for you, the desk and the dog, farther out.
subhead: More square feet in towns farther out, where nearly everything is a drive.
scene: You work at home with space to spare: the typical place found here is about 790 square feet. The evening dog walk reaches a park in about 9 minutes, on streets where 41 percent of homes are houses. On Saturday you drive out, since about 4 restaurants and no bars are within a 10-minute walk. The supermarket is 0.8 miles away. On Sunday the typical place here is about 67 minutes from your parents by car, or about 110 by transit.
promise: More room for you, your desk and the dog, in towns where many neighbors are families.
catch: Your parents are far, typically about 67 minutes each way. Nearly everything is a drive, including the dog park at about 2.3 miles.
host_intro: You work from home, so start with the room you work in: enough for a desk that is separate from the dinner table and a dog with the zoomies. It suits you if home is where you spend your days. You are buying square feet with miles.
host_walkthrough:
A weekday here has elbow room. The desk gets its own corner, the dog gets a park about 9 minutes away, and nobody is working from the couch. Groceries are about 0.8 miles off, so errands mean the car. Most buildings have a gym. The quiet is real, and so is the drive to a decent latte.

Saturday night takes planning. About 10 restaurants sit within 1 mile and bars are scarce, so a night out is a drive there and a sober drive back, or a ride you book ahead. Staying in is the stronger play, because you have space to host. Friends come to you, and the car stays parked.

Sunday is the long haul. The typical drive to your parents is about 67 minutes each way without traffic, and tolls run about $28 round trip with a New York E-ZPass. The closest, Valley Stream, is about 14 minutes out. Transit is about 110 minutes. Pick your town with this drive in mind.
sub_cost: Bills here tend to sit below your limit.
sub_to_parents: Going home is a trip, so you will choose your Sundays.
sub_going_out: Enough for a regular spot, and the rest is a drive.
sub_green: A park is a longer walk here, so the dog's routine takes planning.
sub_compared_to_queens: Compared to staying in Queens, you get bigger rooms and emptier sidewalks.
